### 0.1.0 (2026-10-29) [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-0-2026-10-29)

- `waynestate/helmet` moves from `^0.1` to `^0.2` (locked at 0.2.3). The published `config/helmet.php` re-syncs with the package: `HELMET_PRESET` fills the proxy list (an unknown name throws at boot), and the security headers middleware joins the global chain, so every response carries the baseline. The trusted-header set narrows to `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Forwarded-Proto`; `X-Forwarded-Port` is no longer trusted, because Citadel's HA-Proxy never sends it.
- `php artisan weld:doctor`: local setup only: the app key, writable storage, the database and pending migrations. The standards checks (PHP version, debug in production, secure session cookies) belong to PROCTOR, and the report points at `composer proctor`.
- Ziggy's route list leaves the inline `<script>` from `@routes` and moves into the Vite bundle: `composer ziggy` generates `resources/js/ziggy.js` (plus `ziggy.d.ts`), the app entry imports it and passes it to `ZiggyVue`, so `route()` works in Vue exactly as before while HELMET's strict CSP stays closed. A CI job regenerates the file and fails on any diff, and a feature test pins the contract that every script tag on the app page carries a nonce.
- PROCTOR is welded in from Packagist (`waynestate/proctor` dev dependency, CREED's `policy.json` carried by `waynestate/creed`): `composer proctor` measures WELD against the version policy, and a CI job runs it on every pipeline. Warnings pass, failures block. The package's own bin looks for its autoloader where only a project-root install puts one, so `composer proctor` runs directly without a temporary launcher.
- SESAME is welded in from Packagist (`waynestate/sesame`): sign-in moves from the starter kit's password forms to `/login` and `/logout`, owned by the package. The fake driver signs in locally; pointing at CAS is an env change. A `username` column joins `users`, and `App\Sesame\UserResolver` imports the identity on first sign-in.
- HELMET is welded in from Packagist (`waynestate/helmet`): security headers and CSP on every web response, a published `config/helmet.php`, trusted proxies in `bootstrap/app.php`, and the Vite build asks for the per-request nonce. `/up` stays Laravel's built-in health route. Every web response now wears the baseline.
- `docs/running-off-citadel.md`: the off-Citadel contract: OpenShift, Coolify and plain Docker, with Citadel for comparison. Traffic and trusted proxies per platform, `php://stderr` logs, writable paths, non-root user, `/up`, and `weld:doctor` after every deploy. Same bead, four different tables.
- README: one line under "Run it locally" linking the guide.
- `php artisan weld:doctor`: checks the app is set up safely, one PASS, WARN or FAIL line per check (PHP version, app key, debug in production, secure session cookies, writable storage, database, pending migrations); exits 1 when anything FAILs, `--json` for machines. A good bead is a quiet one: all PASS and nothing to say.
- `bin/weld.ps1` and `bin/weld.sh`: a `doctor` subcommand runs it in the app container.
- README: "Check your setup".
- `compose.yaml`: the local stack: the app (PHP and Composer in one image) and Vite, on pinned images, SQLite per `.env.example`, ports bound to 127.0.0.1 only.
- `bin/weld.ps1` (Windows, PowerShell 5.1 and 7) and `bin/weld.sh` (Linux and macOS, POSIX sh): `up`, `down`, `test` and `logs`, the same subcommands on every OS.
- README: "Run it locally" is now one command per OS.

## Contributing [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#contributing)

This page tells you how to build, test, keep current and release WELD, and where each piece of work belongs.

### Where it lives [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#where-it-lives)

Development happens on git.wayne.edu, the canonical repository: [enterprise-apps/weld](https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/weld). Changes, issues and merge requests go there; tags are made there, by the maintainer, with an approver. The GitHub repository ([waynestate/weld](https://github.com/waynestate/weld)) is a read-only push mirror: `main` and tags are copied automatically, nobody pushes to it, and Packagist reads from it.

Note

The weld is made on git.wayne.edu; the mirrors only get the polished bead.

### Build and test [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#build-and-test)

The Docker path installs, migrates and serves in one command:

sh

```sh
bin/weld.sh up
```

PowerShell

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 up
```

All checks run `composer ci` in the container:

sh

```sh
bin/weld.sh test
```

PowerShell

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 test
```

Check your setup:

sh

```sh
bin/weld.sh doctor
```

PowerShell

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 doctor
```

Logs and stop:

sh

```sh
bin/weld.sh logs
bin/weld.sh down
```

PowerShell

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 logs
.\bin\weld.ps1 down
```

Without Docker: run `composer install`, `npm ci`, copy `.env.example` to `.env`, `php artisan key:generate`, then `composer ci`.

#### Other checks [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#other-checks)

| Check | Command |
| --- | --- |
| PROCTOR against CREED's policy | `composer proctor` |
| Ziggy routes are current | `composer ziggy`, then `git diff --exit-code resources/js/ziggy.*` |
| JS lint, format and types | `npm run lint` (pure check, includes the WayneUI-only import rule), `npm run fix` (apply fixes), `npm run format:check`, `npm run typecheck` |
| Production assets | `npm run build` |

`composer ci` runs `composer validate --strict`, the tests, Pint, PHPStan and `composer audit`. It does not run PROCTOR, Ziggy or the JS lint.

The regen gate checks that WELD is still Sourdough's Inertia shape. Generate a fresh app (`sourdough new <dir> --inertia`), then `php bin/regen-check.php --generated <dir>` (or `composer regen-check -- --generated <dir>`). It skips the product files listed in `.sourdough/product-files.json` and any `vendor` or `node_modules` path, and fails only on drift that is not already recorded in `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json`; `--write-baseline` records the current drift as accepted. It is not part of `composer ci`; CI runs it as a separate job that blocks on new drift.

Pint skips `deploy/`. That folder is the stack's shared front-page deploy layer (Squire kit plus HELMET front controller), kept byte-identical in PER style across every stack repo, so WELD's Laravel preset must not reformat it. Its style is checked where it is made.

### CI [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#ci)

- **GitLab:** Preflight's `php-test` (PHP 8.3, 8.4, 8.5, running `vendor/bin/pest`) and `composer-audit` components, a `composer-ci` job, a `no-dev-install` job (a `composer install --no-dev` that fails if Laravel Boost comes along), a `proctor` job (warnings pass, failures block), a `frontend` job (`npm ci`, lint, Prettier, vue-tsc and the build), a `ziggy` drift job and a `regen-gate` job (new drift fails the job; `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json` records the drift already accepted).
- **GitHub:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` calls Preflight's reusable workflow with `composer ci`, runs the same `frontend` and `no-dev-install` jobs, and runs the same `regen-gate` check (`continue-on-error` until the baseline is filled in).

Green means all of those pass; on GitLab the regen gate blocks on new drift, and on GitHub it may warn while the baseline is being filled in.

### Keeping the joints current [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#keeping-the-joints-current)

- When HELMET, SESAME, CREED or PROCTOR release, raise the constraint here (`composer require waynestate/<part>:^0.x`), run all the checks above, and commit the lock file.
- When Laravel, Inertia or Vue release, Booster's hops are the way to move; WELD is a good first test for them.
- After route changes, regenerate Ziggy and commit the result.
- When Sourdough changes what it generates, the regen gate flags the new drift in CI. Fix it here or upstream in Sourdough; if the drift is accepted as intended, record it with `--write-baseline` and commit `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json`.

### Releasing [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#releasing)

WELD is tagged (0.1.0 through 0.2.1 so far). To cut the next release:

1. Move the lines under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md` to a new `## X.Y.Z (YYYY-MM-DD)` heading.
2. All the checks above green locally, then both pipelines green for that commit.
3. Run a secrets scan of the history and check that nothing internal (server names, people, IDs) is in the tree.
4. Tag `X.Y.Z` (no `v`) on git.wayne.edu, with an approver. The push mirror carries the tag to GitHub.
5. A release needs a maintainer's approval. Never move or delete a published tag.

### Running it elsewhere [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#running-it-elsewhere)

WELD targets Citadel first. [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html) covers OpenShift, Coolify and plain Docker, with Citadel for comparison.

### The front page [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#the-front-page)

`site/` is the stack's front page, for `https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/` on Citadel, served through a small raw-PHP `deploy/` layer generated with Squire (separate from the WELD app itself).

### The docs site [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#the-docs-site)

The docs site is built from `docs/` by the shared docs builder (`composer docs`) and checked by `composer docs:check`. Sources live in `docs/`; the page you read is the page that ships: same source, same bead.

The pages wear the front page's look. The header on every docs page is `docs/_header.html` (keep its links in step with the front page's main menu), and colors, type, callouts and motion live in `docs/theme/weld.css`; `docs/docs.json` names both under `theme`. Change the look there, never in the kit files (`site/assets/docs.css`, `site/assets/docs.js`), which the builder pins by hash.

### Related [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#related)

- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html)

---

Source: https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ai-apps.html

## Building an AI or LLM app [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ai-apps.html#building-an-ai-or-llm-app)

WELD is a working base for an app that talks to a language model: sign-in, sessions, security headers and the checks are already welded in. This page lists the parts that need your attention when the model does the talking. Every rule below comes from the stack's own sources; where behavior depends on your platform, it says so.

### Call the model server-side [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ai-apps.html#call-the-model-server-side)

The browser cannot reach a model API. HELMET's CSP allows `connect-src` only for the app's own origin and the WayneUI CDN (`vendor/waynestate/helmet/src/Headers/SecurityHeaders.php:70`), so a fetch from the page to any other host fails. Make the call from PHP instead, and keep the credential where the page never sees it:

- Put the key in an environment variable and read it in a config file, the way WELD reads every other setting. `config/worker.php:16` shows the pattern: `'mode' => env('QUEUE_WORKER_MODE', 'none')`.
- Never name it `VITE_*`. Vite copies every `VITE_` variable into the built JavaScript: `.env.example:94` feeds `VITE_APP_NAME` from `${APP_NAME}`, and the page reads it back at `resources/js/components/AppHeader.vue:23`. A model key in the bundle is a public key.
- Keep TLS verification on. CREED's handbook, the code chapter, forbids disabling it ([handbook/code.md:70-78](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/handbook/code.md)), and Pinstripe's banned-call rules fail CI on `withoutVerifying()`, `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER` set to false and the rest.

A minimal shape, with the key out of git and out of the bundle:

```php
// config/model.php
return [
    'endpoint' => env('MODEL_ENDPOINT'),
    'api_key' => env('MODEL_API_KEY'),
];
```

```php
$response = Http::withToken(config('model.api_key'))
    ->timeout(60)
    ->post(config('model.endpoint'), ['messages' => $messages]);
```

### Stream the answer [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ai-apps.html#stream-the-answer)

A long answer should not sit in memory until it is complete. Laravel ships both halves of the tool:

- `response()->stream($callback)` sends a chunk as it is produced; with a generator callback it echoes each chunk and flushes after it (`vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Routing/ResponseFactory.php:213,222-228`).
- `response()->eventStream($callback)` does the same as Server-Sent Events, adding `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `Cache-Control: no-cache` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, and flushing after every message (`:146,170-174,198-202`).

Two limits shape how far a stream can run under Citadel's Apache mod_php:

- `output_buffering = 4096` (`deploy/.squire/php.ini:6`) keeps the buffer at 4 KB, so each flush hands over a small unit instead of holding the whole answer.
- `max_execution_time = 30` (`deploy/.squire/php.ini:18`) ends a request that runs longer than 30 seconds. A generation that takes that long needs its work split, or a different limit on your platform: check on your app.

Remember the auth side too: an unauthenticated `text/event-stream` request gets a redirect, not a 401, and `EventSource` cannot follow it ([SESAME and fetch](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#sesame-and-fetch)).

### Store what you learn [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ai-apps.html#store-what-you-learn)

If the app keeps embeddings or model output, it lands in the same shared MySQL 5.6 everything else uses:

- There is no vector column type and no JSON column type on 5.6. CREED's handbook, the databases chapter, says store JSON as `text` or `longText` with Eloquent `array` or `json` casts and filter in PHP ([handbook/databases.md:58-60](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/handbook/databases.md)); PROCTOR's `mysql56` check enforces it.
- WELD already keeps index keys under 5.6's 767-byte cap with `Schema::defaultStringLength(191)` (`app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:32`), and your new tables inherit it.
- Nearest-neighbor search then runs in PHP over the stored rows. That is the price of 5.6; if it stops being cheap, that is a design conversation, not a column type.

### Rate-limit per user [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ai-apps.html#rate-limit-per-user)

Model calls cost money and tokens. Laravel's `RateLimiter` facade (`vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Support/Facades/RateLimiter.php:27`) counts attempts per key; key it on the signed-in user's username, which SESAME's `Identity` carries (`vendor/waynestate/sesame/src/Identity.php:24`):

```php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\RateLimiter;
use Waynestate\Sesame\Sesame;

$user = app(Sesame::class)->user();

if (! RateLimiter::attempt('model:'.$user->username, 30)) {
    abort(429);
}
```

Thirty calls a minute per user is a placeholder, not a policy: pick the number your budget allows.

### Log like everything else [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ai-apps.html#log-like-everything-else)

CREED has no AI-specific logging rules, and the general ones apply:

- Logs and diagnostic output must not contain credentials or personally identifiable information such as Social Security numbers, including logged exceptions (CREED's handbook, the secrets chapter, [handbook/secrets.md:17](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/handbook/secrets.md)). A prompt carrying a student record is personal data: log the size and outcome of a model call, not its full text.
- Logs are rotated or removed at a set interval; on Citadel the platform rotates container logs (CREED's handbook, the production chapter, [handbook/production.md:24](https://github.com/waynestate/creed/blob/main/handbook/production.md)). WELD sends everything to `php://stderr` (`LOG_CHANNEL=stderr`, [Configuration](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)), which is the container log on Citadel.

### Related [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/ai-apps.html#related)

- [Security](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/security.html#the-effective-csp)
- [App structure](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#sesame-and-fetch)
- [Configuration](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)

## App structure [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#app-structure)

This page lists the app structure practices for WELD, from the BEST_PRACTICES guide, with the tag that says whether the stack holds each one today.

### W1. One owner of authentication: SESAME [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#w1-one-owner-of-authentication-sesame)

**Practice:** Remove the Laravel starter kit's Fortify routes and actions (`/login`, `/register`, `/forgot-password`, 2FA). SESAME's `findOrImportUser(Identity)` is the only way in.

**Why:** Two login systems mean two session rules and two audit trails, and the kit's Fortify registers its routes automatically.

**Stack:** `Checked`. SESAME is a dependency (`composer.json:24`), the starter kit's Fortify routes are removed, and `tests/Feature/AuthRoutesTest.php` fails if WELD grows its own auth routes: no register, password, two-factor, forgot, reset, verify or confirm URIs (`:17-30`), no `Laravel\Fortify` actions (`:32-43`), and `/login` and `/logout` owned by SESAME exactly once each (`:45-64`). Open: a PROCTOR check over `php artisan route:list --json`.

### W2. WayneUI is the only component source [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#w2-wayneui-is-the-only-component-source)

**Practice:** Pages use WayneUI components and tokens. Do not keep the kit's shadcn-vue components or Tailwind theme as a second design system.

**Why:** The stack's promise is one interface contract on every consumer path; a parallel component set breaks the accessibility gate.

**Stack:** `Checked`. WayneUI 2.0.8 is the interface: `package.json` pins `@waynestate/wayne-ui-css` and `@waynestate/wayne-ui-vue` exactly (the lock's sha512 integrity is the checksum), `resources/css/app.css` imports the layered `dist/wayne-ui.css`, and the pages and layouts use WayneUI's Vue components (`AppShell`, `AppBar`, `Sidebar`, `Card`, `Input`, `Dialog`, `RadioGroup`). The Tailwind theme, `cn()`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `@headlessui/vue` and `lucide-vue-next` are gone. ESLint's `no-restricted-imports` rule in `eslint.config.js` bans the kit's `components/ui` path and those helpers, `tests/Feature/WayneUiOnlyTest.php` fails when `components.json`, a `components/ui` folder, a Tailwind dependency or a loose WayneUI pin appears, and the `frontend` job in `.gitlab-ci.yml` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs lint, Prettier, vue-tsc and the build. Where WayneUI has no component (the account menu), a small local one is built on its tokens and says so in a comment.

### W3. Own the app code; take stack changes through `sourdough feed` [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#w3-own-the-app-code-take-stack-changes-through-sourdough-feed)

**Practice:** The kit gives you the code ("full ownership"), with no kit upgrade path. WELD's wiring files are marked and refreshed by `sourdough feed`, not hand-edited.

**Why:** Without a feed the app forks from the stack on day one and never gets fixes.

**Stack:** `Checked`. Sourdough is still not a Composer dependency, but a drift gate runs: `bin/regen-check.php` compares WELD file by file by SHA-256 against a fresh `sourdough new --inertia` generation, skips the product files in `.sourdough/product-files.json`, and fails only on new drift versus `.sourdough/regen-baseline.json`. The `regen-gate` jobs in `.gitlab-ci.yml:234-277` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml:56-73` block on new drift. On GitLab the gate always runs on a tag (the release check), on a pipeline schedule and on Run pipeline, and on a push only when the push touches a path the gate compares or the gate itself (`rules:` at `.gitlab-ci.yml:238-251`), so a docs or site push, which cannot cause drift, skips it; the job is `interruptible`, and only its network steps (WELD's and Sourdough's `composer install`, the Sourdough clone) get three tries, so drift is never retried into green. `tests/Unit/RegenGateRulesTest.php` holds the rules. Open: the nightly pipeline schedule on `main` that catches upstream drift (Sourdough's main or the Laravel skeleton moving) when nobody pushes is pending the maintainer's approval, and until it exists that drift shows at WELD's next code push or tag; the gate clones Sourdough's `main` from the GitHub mirror (the job-token clone from git.wayne.edu waits on Sourdough's allowlist), not a pinned stack release.

### W4. Inertia 3 only; migrate off the removed APIs [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#w4-inertia-3-only-migrate-off-the-removed-apis)

**Practice:** Use `@inertiajs/vue3` ^3 and `inertiajs/inertia-laravel` ^3. Do not import Axios, call `Inertia::lazy()` (use `Inertia::optional()`), read `data-page`, or `require()` Inertia packages.

**Why:** Inertia 3 removed all of these; code copied from older tutorials fails or half-works.

**Stack:** `Checked`. WELD is on Inertia 3: `composer.json:19` requires `inertiajs/inertia-laravel: ^3.0` and `package.json:26` requires `@inertiajs/vue3: ^3.0`. `tests/Feature/CspScriptTagsTest.php:53-60` pins the Inertia 3 JSON page island, so a regression to the Inertia 2 layout fails the suite. Open: an ESLint restriction on `axios` and a grep guard for `Inertia::lazy`.

### W5. Commit `.ai/rules`; ignore what Boost regenerates [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#w5-commit-ai-rules-ignore-what-boost-regenerates)

**Practice:** Laravel Boost is a `require-dev` package. Commit `.ai/`: project rules in `.ai/rules/` (with Boost's `index.md`) and WELD's own conventions in `.ai/guidelines/`. Ignore what `boost:install` and `boost:update` write: `.mcp.json`, `boost.json`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/skills/` and `.junie/`. Git cannot ignore only the generated block inside `CLAUDE.md`, so the whole file is ignored and team guidance goes in `.ai/guidelines/`, which Boost folds into every agent's file. `.agents/` stays tracked (Booster's playbooks live there). Each stack package may ship `resources/boost/guidelines/core.blade.php` and `resources/boost/skills/*/SKILL.md`.

**Why:** Rules are shared team memory; generated files change with every `boost:update`, and `boost.json` holds each developer's own agent picks.

**Stack:** `Checked`. `composer.json` requires `laravel/boost: ^2.10` in `require-dev`; `.ai/guidelines/wayne-state.md` and `.ai/rules/` (`index.md`, `migrations.md`, `routes.md`) are committed as Sourdough's Inertia template ships them, and the `.gitignore` carries Sourdough's Boost block. `tests/Feature/BoostDevOnlyTest.php` "ignores what Boost regenerates and keeps what the team shares" fails CI when an ignore line or a committed `.ai` file goes missing, and the regen gate keeps the `.ai` files equal to Sourdough's. Open: a PROCTOR check for apps Sourdough did not bake.

### W6. Sail is local development only [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#w6-sail-is-local-development-only)

**Practice:** Sail's own description is "Laravel's default Docker development environment". It is not a production image and WELD never deploys it.

**Why:** Sail's runtime images carry dev tooling and a bash-script CLI.

**Stack:** `Documented`. `composer.json:33` keeps `laravel/sail` in `require-dev`, so it is a local tool, not a runtime dependency. Target `Checked`: PROCTOR flags `laravel/sail` outside `require-dev` and any `vendor/laravel/sail` path in a production Dockerfile.

### W7. The supported dev path is Compose driven by native scripts, not Sail [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#w7-the-supported-dev-path-is-compose-driven-by-native-scripts-not-sail)

**Practice:** Sail runs on Windows "via WSL2". The stack rule is that Windows needs no bash and no WSL. Ship `weld.ps1` and `weld.sh` (or one PHP command) over a plain `compose.yaml`; Sail stays an unsupported convenience.

**Why:** Every developer OS gets its own native path.

**Stack:** `Checked`. `compose.yaml` and the `bin/weld.ps1` / `bin/weld.sh` pair exist, and `tests/Unit/LocalStackTest.php:10-47` pins the pair's shared behavior: the SQLite file is created only when missing and never truncated, and the Vite service writes a reachable listen address.

### W8. One image, several process types [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#w8-one-image-several-process-types)

**Practice:** Build one image. Run it as `web`, `worker` and `scheduler` by changing the command only (plus `ssr` when Inertia SSR is on). On Compose these are services; on OpenShift a Deployment, a Deployment and a CronJob.

**Why:** One build means one tested artifact, and the process types stay identical in code.

**Stack:** `Checked`, for the portable path. Squire's portable image (`deploy/.squire/portable.Dockerfile`) bakes the code in and runs as `web`, `worker` (`queue:work --tries=3 --max-time=3600 --sleep=3`), `scheduler` (`schedule:work`) or `migrate` by `SQUIRE_ROLE` or the first argument (`deploy/.squire/portable/squire-entrypoint.sh`), and the `portable` profile in `deploy/docker-compose.squire.yml` runs the four as services of one image, the scheduler with `QUEUE_WORKER_MODE: none`. `tests/Feature/PortableImageTest.php` fails when a role, the shared image or that switch goes, and Squire's `PortableImageTest` (`testThePortableProfileRunsOneImageAsFourRoles`, `testTheRolePicksTheProcess`) runs the entrypoint itself. Built and run for real on 2026-11-08: `migrate` exited 0, then `web`, `worker` and `scheduler` came up healthy and the worker ran a queued job. The Citadel mirror (`deploy/.squire/Dockerfile`) still runs Apache only, because Citadel has no worker process (W19). In CI, Preflight's `portability` job (`.gitlab-ci.yml`, Preflight 0.6.0) builds this image and boots its `web` role, the image's default; `tests/Unit/PortabilityJobTest.php` holds the include. Open: no `ssr` role (SSR is off); the `portability` job boots only `web`, so `worker`, `scheduler` and `migrate` run only in the compose profile.

### One-time deploy steps (deployments/) [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#one-time-deploy-steps-deployments)

An app may add its own one-time step as `deployments/002-*.sh`, beside the kit's `001-first-release.sh`. Citadel runs each executable file in `deployments/` once per file name for the life of the app, as the `citadel` user, when the container starts, before Apache (`deploy/deployments/001-first-release.sh:4-5`). A finished file is recorded at `/citadel/logs/deployments/<name>.log` and skipped on later starts; a failed run leaves a `.failed.log` instead, so the next start tries again, up to three times, and then the deployment is marked FAILING (`deploy/.squire/fallback/citadel-deploy:12-14`, `:20-24`; `deploy/deployments/001-first-release.sh:5-6`). Everything in the hook must be safe to run twice (S10). A new file name runs on the next container start after it appears, provided it is executable: the runner takes only executable files (`deploy/.squire/fallback/citadel-deploy:9-10`).

Keep repeatable work in `scripts/release.sh`, which the first-release hook calls with the smoke test off (`deploy/deployments/001-first-release.sh:9-10`, `:25`). Mark a new hook executable in git: `git update-index --chmod=+x deployments/002-your-step.sh`.

Squire's update treats a file it does not pin as yours: `.squire.json` pins the kit's files, including `deployments/001-first-release.sh` (`deploy/.squire.json:28`), and Squire never touches a file it did not write, reports it as `app-owned`, never records or overwrites it, and `init --check` does not count it as drift ([Squire's update-and-drift guide](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/update-and-drift.html)).

### How to read the tags [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#how-to-read-the-tags)

Each practice ends with exactly one tag.

| Tag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Enforced` | WELD's code does it or refuses to run without it, and a test covers it. |
| `Checked` | PROCTOR or CI warns or fails. |
| `Documented` | Written down in the README or a config file, with no check behind it. |
| `Not yet` | A gap. |

### SESAME and fetch [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html#sesame-and-fetch)

The `auth.sesame` middleware lets a request through when SESAME has a user in the session. Otherwise it answers by kind of client (`vendor/waynestate/sesame/src/Laravel/Authenticate.php:25-36`):

- a request for which Laravel's `expectsJson()` is true gets **401** with the body `Unauthorized.` (`:31-33`);
- everything else gets **redirected to the login route**, `GET /login` (`:35`, registered at `vendor/waynestate/sesame/src/Laravel/SesameServiceProvider.php:297`).

Laravel's `expectsJson()` is true when the first type in `Accept` is JSON (`.../json` or `...+json`), or when the request carries `X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest`, is not pjax, and accepts any content type (`vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Http/Concerns/InteractsWithContentTypes.php:24-27,34-39,136-143`). Two consequences for scripted requests:

- A bare `fetch('/api/answer')` sends `Accept: */*` and no XHR header, so it is not a JSON request and gets the redirect, not a 401. Send the JSON Accept header and handle the 401:
  ```js
  const res = await fetch('/api/answer', { headers: { Accept: 'application/json' } });
  if (res.status === 401) {
    // signed out: send the browser to /login
  }
  ```
- A streaming `text/event-stream` request is never JSON: its first type is not JSON, and `X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest` only counts when the request accepts any content type. An unauthenticated stream therefore gets the redirect, and `EventSource` cannot follow one. Check the session before opening the stream, or treat a redirect as signed out.

## Build and supply chain [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/build-and-supply-chain.html#build-and-supply-chain)

This page states WELD's build and supply chain practices, one per heading, each with the rule and the tag that shows whether the stack holds it today.

### W30: Support only PHP versions that are not end of life [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/build-and-supply-chain.html#w30-support-only-php-versions-that-are-not-end-of-life)

**Practice:** `composer.json` requires `php: ^8.3` with `config.platform.php` `8.3.0`. Tests run on 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5. Laravel 13 needs 8.3 or newer.

**Stack:** `Checked`. `composer.json:18` requires `php: ^8.3`, `composer.json:134` sets `config.platform.php` to `8.3.0`, and the CI matrix runs on 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 (`.gitlab-ci.yml:9` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml:18`).

### W31: Keep dev tools inside the PHP floor [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/build-and-supply-chain.html#w31-keep-dev-tools-inside-the-php-floor)

**Practice:** Pest 5 requires PHP `^8.4`. On a `^8.3` floor use Pest 4 or PHPUnit and cap the constraint.

**Stack:** `Checked`. WELD adopted Pest 4 on 2026-11-03: `composer.json` requires `pestphp/pest ^4` (Pest 5 needs PHP `^8.4`), and the CI matrix starts at 8.3 (`.gitlab-ci.yml:9`), so `composer install` runs on 8.3 and fails if a dev tool requires 8.4 or newer. The PHPUnit class tests still run unchanged, under Pest, and new tests are written in Pest.

### W32: Pinstripe owns style and static analysis [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/build-and-supply-chain.html#w32-pinstripe-owns-style-and-static-analysis)

**Practice:** Use Pinstripe's Pint preset, PHPStan level 8 through Larastan, ESLint (flat config) and Prettier. No local overrides without a recorded reason.

**Stack:** `Checked`, for the PHP side. `waynestate/pinstripe` `^0.3` is a dev dependency (`composer.json:43`), and `phpstan.neon:10` includes its `phpstan/laravel.neon`, so level 8, the ignore rules and the banned calls (SQL joined from strings among them) come from the package; WELD's code passes with no new ignore and no baseline. `composer.json:60` runs `pint --test`, `composer.json:63` runs `phpstan analyse`, and both are in the `ci` script (`composer.json:68-77`), which CI runs. `pint.json` is Pinstripe's `pint/laravel.json` plus two recorded excludes, Squire's `deploy/` kit and `bin/docs-site.php`, since Pint cannot extend a config file; `tests/Unit/PinstripeWiringTest.php` fails on any other drift in either file. The JS side runs in CI too, on WELD's own config until `@waynestate/pinstripe` 0.3.0 is on npm: the `frontend` job (`.gitlab-ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs `npm run lint` (`eslint.config.js`, flat config) and `npm run format:check` (`.prettierrc`).

### W33: Pin shared CI components to a commit [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/build-and-supply-chain.html#w33-pin-shared-ci-components-to-a-commit)

**Practice:** Preflight components are referenced by commit SHA or a fixed tag, not a moving branch.

**Stack:** `Checked`. `.gitlab-ci.yml` pins every Preflight component to the 0.8.0 release tag (`@0.8.0` at `.gitlab-ci.yml:7`, `:15`, `:18`, `:26`, `:35`, `:45`, `:49`, `:56`, `:80`; published tags in the stack never move), and `.github/workflows/ci.yml:16` calls Preflight 0.8.0's reusable workflow at its release commit (`28d9c5994d06c633850d431dcf6ca56c48a96055`). PROCTOR's `preflight-pinned` check, run by the `proctor-root` job (`composer proctor`), warns on an include without a full release tag or a commit SHA.

## Check your setup [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html#check-your-setup)

Use `weld:doctor` to strike an arc across the local setup and see, one line per check, whether every joint holds.

### What it checks [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html#what-it-checks)

`weld:doctor` strikes an arc across the local setup and reports every joint: the app key, writable storage, the database and pending migrations. One line per check, PASS or WARN or FAIL. The checks, by name:

- `app-key`: PASS when `APP_KEY` is set; FAIL when it is empty, with a pointer to `php artisan key:generate`.
- `storage-writable`: PASS when `storage` and `bootstrap/cache` are both writable; FAIL when either is missing or not writable.
- `database`: PASS when the connection is up; FAIL names the exception class only, never the DSN, host or password.
- `migrations`: PASS when there are no pending migrations; WARN when some are pending (it lists them) or when it could not inspect them.

### Run it [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html#run-it)

Run it through the OS scripts or straight to the container:

PowerShell

```powershell
.\bin\weld.ps1 doctor
```

macOS / Linux

```sh
bin/weld.sh doctor
```

Container

```sh
docker compose run --rm app php artisan weld:doctor
```

### Read the report [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html#read-the-report)

Each check prints one line: PASS, WARN or FAIL. The exit code is 1 when anything FAILs and 0 otherwise, so it works as a gate. Add `--json` to any of them for a machine-readable report. A good bead is a quiet one: all PASS and nothing to say.

Note

The standards checks (PHP version, debug in production, secure session cookies) belong to PROCTOR: run `composer proctor`, and the doctor report says so.

Not sure whether you want `weld:doctor`, `squire doctor` or `proctor check`? [Which command when](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/which-command.html) puts every look-alike side by side.

### Related [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html#related)

- [Which command when](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/which-command.html)
- [What is welded in](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html)
- [Oracle](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html)
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html)

## Citadel limits [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel-limits.html#citadel-limits)

This page lists the platform facts an app design depends on when it runs on Citadel, each with its source. Design around them and the deploy is a formality; discover them at deploy time and the weld cracks.

### MySQL 5.6.51 [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel-limits.html#mysql-5-6-51)

Citadel shares one MySQL 5.6.51 server. Two limits bite at design time:

- No JSON or `vector` columns. Store JSON as `text` or `longText` with an Eloquent `array` or `json` cast, and filter in PHP (CREED's databases handbook).
- Indexed utf8mb4 strings at most 191 characters. `Schema::defaultStringLength(191)` keeps index keys under the 767-byte cap; WELD sets it in `app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:32`.

The `mysql56-migrate` job runs `php artisan migrate` against a real 5.6.51 service on every pipeline, because the SQLite tests take a JSON column or a long utf8mb4 index that 5.6 rejects at deploy (`.gitlab-ci.yml:50-56`).

### No separate queue worker [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel-limits.html#no-separate-queue-worker)

Citadel runs no queue worker process. The scheduler drains the queue instead: `QUEUE_WORKER_MODE=scheduler` (the `.env.example` default) schedules a short `queue:work --stop-when-empty --max-time=50 --tries=3` every minute (W19, `docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.md:20-24`; `docs/running-off-citadel.md:46`). Design jobs to be short; do not assume a long-lived worker.

### No sidecars [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel-limits.html#no-sidecars)

One container per app. WELD deploys on Citadel through Squire as one container per app, and builds run at release time inside the app container (`docs/running-off-citadel.md:8`); traffic comes in through Citadel's front-end proxy, HA-Proxy (`docs/running-off-citadel.md:40`). The database is the one Citadel shares, the queue rides the scheduler, and the proxy sits in front; nothing runs beside the app.

### Squire's php.ini limits [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel-limits.html#squire-s-php-ini-limits)

Squire's `php.ini` (the safe defaults HELMET also enforces at runtime) sets, among others:

- `memory_limit = 128M` (`deploy/.squire/php.ini:20`)
- `max_execution_time = 30` (`deploy/.squire/php.ini:18`)
- `output_buffering = 4096` (`deploy/.squire/php.ini:6`)

Size uploads and long-running work around them.

### Related [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel-limits.html#related)

## The container contract [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#the-container-contract)

This page lists the container contract practices for WELD, from the BEST_PRACTICES guide, with the tag that says whether the stack holds each one today.

### W9. Config comes from the environment only [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w9-config-comes-from-the-environment-only)

**Practice:** No `.env` in the image. Call `env()` only inside `config/*.php`.

**Why:** After `config:cache` the `.env` file is not loaded and `env()` returns `null` elsewhere.

**Stack:** `Checked`. Every `env()` call is inside `config/*.php` except one documented exception: `bootstrap/app.php:44` reads `TRUSTED_PROXIES` because the middleware closure runs before config is loaded, and carries a `@phpstan-ignore` for `larastan.noEnvCallsOutsideOfConfig`. That rule is live (`phpstan.neon:10` sets `reportUnmatchedIgnoredErrors: true`), and `phpstan analyse` runs in the `ci` script (`composer.json:61`, `:66-75`), so a new `env()` outside `config/` fails CI.

### W10. `config:cache` runs at container start, never at image build [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w10-config-cache-runs-at-container-start-never-at-image-build)

**Practice:** Build time may run `route:cache`, `view:cache`, `event:cache`. `php artisan optimize` at start is acceptable if the build did not freeze config.

**Why:** A build-time `config:cache` freezes the build machine's environment into the image.

**Stack:** `Checked`. The image build runs no artisan commands: `deploy/build.sh:49-51` fails if app source is present at build time, and the release step runs `php artisan optimize` once the environment is in place (`deploy/scripts/release.sh:555-561`), so config is cached at deploy, never at build. The portable image runs the release script with `SQUIRE_ARTISAN_OPTIMIZE=0` at build (`deploy/.squire/portable.Dockerfile`), and its entrypoint runs `php artisan optimize` when a container starts. Preflight's `portability` job (`.gitlab-ci.yml`) fails when that image ships `bootstrap/cache/config.php` or a `.env` (its `env-only` check), and then boots it on the environment alone; `tests/Unit/PortabilityJobTest.php` holds the include. Open: nothing scans the Citadel mirror's Dockerfile, which `build.sh`'s source check covers instead.

### W11. `/up` is the liveness endpoint, and it never checks the database [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w11-up-is-the-liveness-endpoint-and-it-never-checks-the-database)

**Practice:** Keep Laravel's `/up` (200 when the app boots). It must answer for any `Host`, over plain HTTP, before trusted hosts, redirects, sessions, CSP and auth. Put database and cache checks on a separate `/ready` endpoint, through the `DiagnosingHealth` event or a package.

**Why:** A database blip must not make the orchestrator kill every web container.

**Stack:** `Checked`. `bootstrap/app.php:20` sets the health route to `/up`, and `tests/Feature/HelmetHeadersTest.php:41-51` fails the suite when `/up` stops answering 200, and `tests/Feature/HealthHostTest.php` proves it answers 200 for a forged or IP `Host` with no cookie and no redirect. `/ready` is a separate route, HELMET's `Route::helmetReady()` registered in the routing `then:` callback outside the web group (`bootstrap/app.php:27-33`), so a probe writes no session row and sets no cookie. It checks the database (`app/Health/DatabaseReady.php` opens the default connection), the cache (`app/Health/CacheReady.php` writes a key, reads it back and forgets it) and the scheduler heartbeat (W23), and answers 503 when one fails. `tests/Feature/ReadyChecksTest.php` proves it: "answers 503 on /ready when the database cannot be reached" (a missing SQLite file), "answers 503 on /ready when the cache store fails" (a store with no driver), "serves /ready outside the web group, with no session cookie" and "keeps /up free of the readiness checks" (the same broken database, and `/up` still answers 200). The checks and the test are byte for byte from Sourdough's Inertia shape; the route lines join WELD's own `bootstrap/app.php` and `routes/web.php`, which the regen baseline already accepts as drift. The checks use Laravel's own `DB` and `Cache` rather than the `DiagnosingHealth` event or a package, because HELMET's route already gives each check a name, a status and a logged reason.

### W12. Image health check matches the platform [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w12-image-health-check-matches-the-platform)

**Practice:** Put a `HEALTHCHECK` in the Dockerfile that calls `/up` with a tool the image has (`curl` or `wget`). On Coolify a Dockerfile `HEALTHCHECK` takes precedence over the dashboard check, and a dashboard check needs `curl` or `wget` inside the container.

**Why:** Traefik will not route to an unhealthy container, and a missing tool makes a healthy app look dead.

**Stack:** `Checked`. The Dockerfile carries a `HEALTHCHECK` (`deploy/.squire/Dockerfile:47`) whose script asks the local web server for `/up` by default and reads no database (`deploy/health.php:27`, `deploy/health.php:13`); the portable image's `HEALTHCHECK` runs `squire-entrypoint health`, the same script. Preflight's `portability` job (`.gitlab-ci.yml`) builds with `--format docker`, so the image keeps its `HEALTHCHECK`. Its `healthcheck` check runs that command inside the booted replica, as the app's uid, and fails on a non-zero exit. `require_healthcheck: true` fails it if the Dockerfile stops declaring one. `tests/Unit/PortabilityJobTest.php` holds the inputs.

### W13. Non-root, arbitrary UID in group 0, listen on 8080 [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w13-non-root-arbitrary-uid-in-group-0-listen-on-8080)

**Practice:** Declare a non-root `USER`. Make writable paths group 0 and group-writable (`chgrp -R 0`, `chmod -R g=u`) for `storage/` and `bootstrap/cache/`. Do not depend on a `www-data` entry. Honor `PORT`.

**Why:** OpenShift runs a random UID in group 0 with all capabilities dropped.

**Stack:** `Checked`, for the portable path. `deploy/.squire/portable.Dockerfile` declares `USER 10001:0` (no `/etc/passwd` entry, no `www-data`), hands Apache's run, lock and log folders and `storage/` and `bootstrap/cache/` to group 0 with `chmod -R g=u`, and Apache listens on `SQUIRE_PORT`, else `PORT`, else 8080 (`deploy/.squire/portable/ports.conf`, `deploy/.squire/portable/vhost.conf`); the entrypoint refuses a port below 1024 for a user that is not root. The compose profile runs it with `cap_drop: [ALL]` and `no-new-privileges`. `tests/Feature/PortableImageTest.php` holds the user, the group-0 folders and the port in WELD's copy, and Squire's `PortableImageTest` (`testThePortableImageRunsAsANumericNonRootUserInGroupZeroOn8080`, `testABadSettingStopsTheContainerWithAPlainMessage`) checks the kit. Run for real on 2026-11-08 as `--user 1000123:0`, the way OpenShift would: `/up` answered 200 on 8080 and `storage/` was writable. The Citadel image is not this image: it starts as root and drops to its own user, and its vhost stays on 80 (`deploy/.squire/vhost.conf:2`). In CI, Preflight's `portability` job (`.gitlab-ci.yml`) starts the image as `100123:0`, a uid with no `/etc/passwd` entry, with every capability dropped, and its `strict-boot` check fails when the app root is writable by that user, when `storage/` or `bootstrap/cache/` is not, when a second replica does not listen on `PORT=8081`, or when the app writes anywhere but those folders and the tmpfs paths. The job builds from a checkout whose files a Docker executor makes world-writable, so it puts the modes back first (`chmod -R go-w .`). Open: the base image's inherited `EXPOSE 80` still shows in the metadata; the job emulates a read-only root filesystem (it looks for writes after the run) rather than mounting one.

### W14. Logs go to stderr; the app writes only where it may [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w14-logs-go-to-stderr-the-app-writes-only-where-it-may)

**Practice:** Set `LOG_CHANNEL=stderr`. Nothing under `storage/logs`. Writes go to `storage/`, `bootstrap/cache/`, `/tmp` and declared volumes. Uploads go to object storage.

**Why:** Platforms collect stdout/stderr; local files vanish with the container.

**Stack:** `Checked`. `.env.example:18` sets `LOG_CHANNEL=stderr`, and the portable image's Apache logs to the container's stdout and stderr (`deploy/.squire/portable/vhost.conf`). Preflight's `portability` job (`.gitlab-ci.yml`) boots the image and fails when nothing reaches stdout or stderr, when anything is written under `storage/logs` (its `logs` check), or when anything is written outside `storage/`, `bootstrap/cache/` and the tmpfs paths (`strict-boot`); `tests/Unit/PortabilityJobTest.php` holds the include. Open: nothing checks that uploads go to object storage.

### W15. Sessions and cache live in a shared store [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w15-sessions-and-cache-live-in-a-shared-store)

**Practice:** Use `SESSION_DRIVER=database` (or Redis) and a shared cache, even for one replica. Every host overlaps old and new containers during a deploy.

**Why:** A login must survive a hop between replicas.

**Stack:** `Checked`. `.env.example:38` sets `SESSION_DRIVER=database` and `.env.example:69` sets `CACHE_STORE=database`; `config/session.php:21` and `config/cache.php:18` default to the same. Preflight's `portability` job (`.gitlab-ci.yml`) starts a MySQL 8.4 both replicas share (`services`, `.gitlab-ci.yml:109`), migrates it once before they boot (`setup_command`), and runs with `SESSION_DRIVER=database` and `CACHE_STORE=database`; its `session-hop` check signs in on replica A through `/_portability/login` and reads the session on replica B through `/_portability/me` (`routes/web.php`, present only when `PORTABILITY_PROBE=yes`, proven absent by default in `tests/Feature/PortabilityProbeRoutesTest.php`). `tests/Unit/PortabilityJobTest.php` holds the inputs.

### W16. Stop cleanly on SIGTERM [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w16-stop-cleanly-on-sigterm)

**Practice:** Run PHP as PID 1 under a small init, or an entrypoint that `exec`s the server. Queue workers finish the current job on `SIGTERM`. Set the platform's grace period above the longest job `#[Timeout]`.

**Why:** A hard kill mid-job double-runs it after `retry_after`.

**Stack:** `Checked`, for the portable `web` role. The entrypoint replaces the shell with the server (`deploy/.squire/fallback/citadel-apache-entrypoint:58`), so `SIGTERM` reaches the foreground process directly. On the portable path the image sets `STOPSIGNAL SIGTERM`: the `web` role turns it into Apache's graceful stop and the `worker` and `scheduler` roles exec PHP, which finishes the current job (Squire's `testSigtermIsAGracefulStopForApacheAndItsStatusIsTheContainers`; on 2026-11-08 `docker stop` ended all three in about two seconds with exit 0). Preflight's `portability` job (`.gitlab-ci.yml`) sends `SIGTERM` to the booted `web` role's main process and fails unless that process has a handler for it and exits by itself within 10 seconds (its `sigterm` check), which is what PID 1 needs. The job runs the image's own entrypoint with no `start_command`: since Preflight 0.5.0 its launcher starts each replica in a session of its own, as a container is, so Apache's graceful stop reaches only Apache. `tests/Unit/PortabilityJobTest.php` holds the include. The grace period is a platform setting. Open: CI does not stop a `worker` or `scheduler` mid-job.

### W17. Trust proxies by preset, never `*` [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#w17-trust-proxies-by-preset-never)

**Practice:** Select a HELMET preset (`citadel` or `docker`), or list the front proxy in `HELMET_PROXIES` on other platforms. Do not paste `trustProxies(at: '*')` from tutorials. Set `APP_URL` and trusted hosts; Laravel trusts subdomains of `APP_URL` unless `subdomains: false`.

**Why:** An app that trusts all proxies lets a client forge `X-Forwarded-*` and the host used in callbacks.

**Stack:** `Enforced` by HELMET 1.3 (required `^1.3`): it trusts only the preset or listed proxies and drops `X-Forwarded-Port`. CI checks it too: Preflight's `portability` job (`.gitlab-ci.yml`) boots the image with `TRUSTED_PROXIES` and `HELMET_PROXIES` set empty, sends `/dashboard` forged `X-Forwarded-Host`, `-Proto`, `-Port` and `X-Forwarded-User` from that untrusted peer, and fails if the status or the `Location` of the guest redirect changes or a forged value shows up in the answer (its `forwarded-headers` check).

### How to read the tags [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html#how-to-read-the-tags)

Each practice ends with exactly one tag.

| Tag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Enforced` | WELD's code does it or refuses to run without it, and a test covers it. |
| `Checked` | PROCTOR or CI warns or fails. |
| `Documented` | Written down in the README or a config file, with no check behind it. |
| `Not yet` | A gap. |

## Making WELD yours [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/making-weld-yours.html#making-weld-yours)

WELD is built to be cloned: rename it, strip what is WELD's own, and keep the stack underneath. New kitchen, same dough.

### Rename the parts that still say WELD [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/making-weld-yours.html#rename-the-parts-that-still-say-weld)

| Where | What to change |
| --- | --- |
| `.env` | `APP_NAME` (`.env.example:1`). `VITE_APP_NAME` follows on its own: `.env.example:94` sets it from `${APP_NAME}`. |
| `composer.json` | `name` (`:3`), `description` (`:5`), `homepage` (`:6`) and `support` (`:7-10`) |
| `package.json` | `name` (`:2`) |
| Site title | `resources/views/app.blade.php:30` reads `config('app.name')`, which is `APP_NAME` (`config/app.php:16`); the literal `WELD` there is only the fallback for when the variable is unset |
| Header brand | `resources/js/components/AppHeader.vue:23` falls back to `WELD` when `VITE_APP_NAME` is unset |
| Git remote | `git remote set-url origin <your repo>` |

Then give the copy its own key (`php artisan key:generate`) and re-run the checks. A case-insensitive grep finds the stragglers: `git grep -in weld`. Two are internal names, not user-facing: the `weld-form` class in `resources/js/components/DeleteUser.vue:48,58`, and the npm name above.

### Strip WELD's product files [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/making-weld-yours.html#strip-weld-s-product-files)

WELD's drift gate lists its own product files in `.sourdough/product-files.json:1-19`: `site/`, `docs/`, `deploy/`, `bin/`, `scripts/readme-art/`, `compose.yaml`, `compose.oracle.yaml`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `MAINTAINING.md`, `BEST_PRACTICES.md`, `LICENSE`, `README.md`, `agent-ready.json`, `.github/`, `composer.lock`, `package-lock.json` and `.env`. A derived app usually strips the documentation and the site (`site/`, `docs/`, `bin/`, `BEST_PRACTICES.md`, the `.sourdough/` drift-gate files) and keeps the rest: `deploy/` is how it reaches Citadel, and `compose.yaml` is how it runs locally.

The stripping has to reach the tooling that points at the stripped files, or `composer ci` fails at `@test` or at the check steps:

- Drop the three `ci` entries that run the docs and site checks: `@site:agent-ready-check`, `@docs:practices-check` and `@docs:check` (`composer.json:73-75`), with their script definitions (`composer.json:78-83`) and the standalone `regen-check` script (`composer.json:66`).
- Drop the tests that exist only to guard the stripped files: `tests/Unit/FrontPageReleasesTest.php` reads `site/index.html`, `tests/Unit/PracticesCoverageTest.php` checks that `docs/guides/*.md` covers every practice in `BEST_PRACTICES.md`, `tests/Unit/RegenGateRulesTest.php` parses the `regen-gate` job out of `.gitlab-ci.yml`, and `tests/Unit/LocalStackTest.php` reads `bin/weld.ps1` and `bin/weld.sh`.
- `pint.json` records two extra excludes, `deploy/` and `bin/docs-site.php` (`tests/Unit/PinstripeWiringTest.php:43-48` holds the pairing): drop the exclude for a file you drop.

The rule under all of it: a test that reads a file fails when the file goes, so the test goes with the file.

### Adopt with Sourdough so feed keeps working [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/making-weld-yours.html#adopt-with-sourdough-so-feed-keeps-working)

`sourdough feed` only reaches an app that carries `.sourdough/manifest.json`, and `sourdough new` writes one only into the apps it bakes (Sourdough's [adopt guide](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/main/docs/guides/adopt.md), opening paragraph). WELD itself is not adopted: it was built by hand and checks its drift against a fresh Inertia bake with its own regen check (adopt guide, "When to adopt"), so a clone of WELD has no manifest, and `feed` answers exit `2` with the way in (Sourdough's [keeping-current guide](https://github.com/waynestate/sourdough/blob/main/docs/guides/keeping-current.md), "Apps Sourdough did not make, and WELD").

Run adopt once, in the renamed copy, on a clean git tree:

```
sourdough adopt --shape laravel-inertia --dry-run
sourdough adopt --shape laravel-inertia --name your-app
git add .sourdough && git commit -m "Adopt with Sourdough"
sourdough feed --dry-run
```

The shape name is `laravel-inertia`; `--inertia` is the flag `sourdough new` takes, and adopt resolves the name against the five shapes. What adopt does and does not touch:

- It writes one file, `.sourdough/manifest.json`, and never changes your code (adopt guide, opening paragraph).
- Files the template does not ship are not recorded: Sourdough never reads or touches them (adopt guide, "Read the report"). Whether you adopt before or after stripping the product files makes no difference to the manifest.
- `--name` defaults to the folder's basename; the template writes the name into `composer.json`, `public/index.php` and the README (adopt guide, "Pick the shape and the name"). Because you renamed first, those files land in `yours`, and feed never writes, merges or deletes a `yours` file.
- Files that match the template become `managed` and get every template update; files the app lacks arrive with the first feed (adopt guide, "Look first").

One CI note: WELD's pipeline carries the regen gate, not the feed job (`.gitlab-ci.yml:214`), so nothing warns when your app falls behind its template. Copy the `sourdough-feed` job from a fresh bake of the same shape if you want the warning (adopt guide, "Your own .gitlab-ci.yml").

### Related [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/making-weld-yours.html#related)

- [Quick start](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html)
- [WELD and Sourdough](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/sourdough.html)
- [Is WELD still Sourdough's shape?](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/regen-check.html)

## Oracle [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#oracle)

Set up and check WELD's Oracle connection: the settings, the plain-language check, and the parity image for a real connection from your machine.

### The wiring [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#the-wiring)

WELD speaks Oracle through `yajra/laravel-oci8`, and the wiring is already in: an `oracle` connection in `config/database.php`, a check command, and plain-language sentences for the common errors. Until you set the Oracle settings it stays dormant: nothing connects and nothing errors.

### Set the settings [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#set-the-settings)

Fill in one set of names in `.env` (the commented block in `.env.example`): `ORACLE_USERNAME`, `ORACLE_PASSWORD`, and either `ORACLE_TNS` (an Easy Connect string, `host:port/service`, or a full descriptor) or `ORACLE_HOST`, `ORACLE_PORT` and `ORACLE_SERVICE_NAME`. Leave them empty if your app does not use Oracle; nothing connects until they are set. On a server, set them in the app's environment settings, never in a file in git.

### Check the connection [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#check-the-connection)

Check the settings and the connection in plain language, one line per finding:

```
php artisan oracle:check
```

`oracle:check` is a thin wire to Squire's shared check file: it runs `deploy/oracle-check.php` with the current environment, streams the plain-language lines straight through, and returns the check's exit code, 0 when Oracle is not configured or all passed and 1 when a problem was found. The check file promises to never print a setting value. WELD does not own the check; a kit refresh (`vendor/bin/squire update`) puts the file here. If the check file is not there yet, the command tells you to run `vendor/bin/squire update` to get it.

### A real connection from your machine [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#a-real-connection-from-your-machine)

The local `app` container runs the stock Composer image, which has no Oracle driver. When you need a real connection from your machine, the Oracle-ready image is opt-in through `compose.oracle.yaml`:

PowerShell

```powershell
$env:WELD_ORACLE_IMAGE = "squire/oracle-parity:8.3"
docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.oracle.yaml up
```

macOS / Linux

```sh
WELD_ORACLE_IMAGE=squire/oracle-parity:8.3 docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.oracle.yaml up
```

The overlay swaps only the app's image and passes the `ORACLE_*` settings through from `.env`; the ports stay bound to `127.0.0.1`. It fails closed when `WELD_ORACLE_IMAGE` is unset.

`squire/oracle-parity:8.3` is the name Squire documents for its parity image; build it once with Squire's `scripts/oracle-image-build.sh --flavour parity --php 8.3` (the name is a placeholder until a registry is chosen).

Or skip the overlay: Citadel's own PHP image carries `oci8`, so [running WELD like Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#run-it-like-citadel) with Parity reaches Oracle the way the deployed app will (Parity's `--fallback` stand-in leaves `oci8` out).

### Related [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#related)

- [What is welded in](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html)
- [Check your setup](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html)
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html)

Source: https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html

## Queues and scheduling [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#queues-and-scheduling)

This page lists the queue and scheduling practices for WELD without Citadel workers, from the BEST_PRACTICES guide, with the tag that says whether the stack holds each one today.

### W18. Database queue by default; the worker is a process type [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w18-database-queue-by-default-the-worker-is-a-process-type)

**Practice:** `QUEUE_CONNECTION=database`; run `php artisan queue:work --max-time=3600 --tries=3` as the `worker` process where the platform allows one. Use `#[Tries]`, `#[Timeout]` and `#[Backoff]` on jobs.

**Why:** It needs no extra service, and `--max-time` recycles memory.

**Stack:** `Checked` for the job attributes. `.env.example:67` sets `QUEUE_CONNECTION=database`, `config/queue.php:16` defaults to it, and the jobs tables are migrated by `database/migrations/0001_01_01_000002_create_jobs_table.php:14`. `tests/Feature/JobLimitsTest.php` fails the suite on a queued job under `app/Jobs` without `#[Tries]` and `#[Timeout]` (on the class, a parent or a trait; the older `$tries` and `$timeout` properties count too), proves the guard on fixture jobs, and passes while there are no jobs, which is WELD today. `stubs/job.queued.stub` and `stubs/job.batched.queued.stub` make `php artisan make:job` write `#[Tries(3)]` and `#[Timeout(45)]`. Byte for byte from Sourdough's Inertia shape, held by the regen gate. The worker process type is the portable image's `worker` role (`queue:work --tries=3 --max-time=3600`, W8). Open: nothing asks for `#[Backoff]`, so a failed job retries at once unless it sets one.

### W19. Where no worker can run, run the queue from the scheduler [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w19-where-no-worker-can-run-run-the-queue-from-the-scheduler)

**Practice:** On Citadel (no queue workers), schedule `queue:work --stop-when-empty --max-time=50 --timeout=45 --tries=3` every minute with `withoutOverlapping` and a short expiry. Select it with `QUEUE_WORKER_MODE=scheduler` (`none` leaves the queue to a supervisor).

**Why:** `--stop-when-empty` is documented for Docker use ("shutdown the container after the queue is empty"), and the scheduler is the one cron entry Citadel can run. This exact pattern is an inference, not a documented recipe.

**Stack:** `Checked`. `routes/console.php` schedules `queue:work --stop-when-empty --max-time=50 --timeout=45 --tries=3` every minute with `withoutOverlapping(10)` when `config('worker.mode')` is `scheduler` (`config/worker.php`, env `QUEUE_WORKER_MODE`, default `scheduler` in `.env.example`); `tests/Feature/QueueWorkerScheduleTest.php` checks both modes. Byte for byte from Sourdough, held by the regen gate.

### W20. Timeout below `retry_after` [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w20-timeout-below-retry-after)

**Practice:** Set each job timeout lower than the connection's `retry_after`. Timeouts need the PCNTL extension.

**Why:** Otherwise the job is attempted again before it has finished.

**Stack:** `Checked`. `routes/console.php` passes `--timeout=45`, and `tests/Feature/QueueWorkerScheduleTest.php` fails when that is not below the default connection's `retry_after` (or, for `sync`, below every connection's; Laravel's default is 90). Each job's own timeout is held the same way: `tests/Feature/JobLimitsTest.php` fails on a job under `app/Jobs` whose `#[Timeout]` (or `$timeout`) is at or above that `retry_after` ("keeps every job timeout below the queue connection retry_after"; "catches a job timeout at or above retry_after" proves it on a 600-second fixture), and holds the `make:job` stubs' 45 below it too. The deploy image installs `pcntl` (`deploy/.squire/base-fallback.Dockerfile`). Byte for byte from Sourdough, held by the regen gate.

### W21. One scheduler entry; one run per task [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w21-one-scheduler-entry-one-run-per-task)

**Practice:** Run `php artisan schedule:run` every minute (cron, or a CronJob), or `schedule:work` for a single long-lived container. With more than one scheduler, mark tasks `onOneServer()` (shared cache) and name closures.

**Why:** Three schedulers run a nightly report three times.

**Stack:** `Checked`. `tests/Feature/SchedulerNamingTest.php` (Sourdough's copy) fails the suite on any scheduled closure without `->name()`, and its second case proves the guard catches one.

### W22. Interrupt and restart long-lived processes at deploy [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w22-interrupt-and-restart-long-lived-processes-at-deploy)

**Practice:** After a release run `php artisan queue:restart` (or `php artisan reload`), and `schedule:interrupt` when sub-minute tasks exist.

**Why:** Workers and a minute-long `schedule:run` keep the old code until they exit.

**Stack:** `Checked`. The Squire release step "laravel restart long-lived processes" (`deploy/scripts/release.sh:563`) runs `php artisan reload` where Laravel has it, otherwise `queue:restart` and `schedule:interrupt`, each when its own `--help` answers; report only, and `SQUIRE_ARTISAN_RESTART=0` turns the step off. `tests/Feature/ReleaseRestartTest.php` holds the commands and the switch in place.

### W23. Make a silent scheduler visible [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w23-make-a-silent-scheduler-visible)

**Practice:** Record a heartbeat on every scheduler minute and fail `/ready` (not `/up`) when it is older than a few minutes. Export the age as a Prometheus gauge (off by default).

**Why:** With no worker supervisor, a stopped scheduler is otherwise invisible.

**Stack:** `Checked` for the heartbeat. `routes/console.php:17-19` stamps the cache every minute in a closure named `scheduler-heartbeat`, and `bootstrap/app.php:31` puts `App\Health\SchedulerHeartbeat` on HELMET's `/ready` beside the database and cache checks (W11), which answers 503 while the stamp is missing or older than `worker.heartbeat_max_age` (`config/worker.php:31`, env `WORKER_HEARTBEAT_MAX_AGE`, default 180 seconds; 0 turns the check off for an app that runs no scheduler). `tests/Feature/SchedulerHeartbeatTest.php` proves it: "answers 503 on /ready when the scheduler has not written a heartbeat", "answers 200 on /ready right after the heartbeat closure runs", "answers 503 on /ready again once the clock moves past the max age" (the fake clock), "answers 200 on /ready with no heartbeat when the check is turned off" and "schedules the heartbeat every minute under its own name". Byte for byte from Sourdough, held by the regen gate. Open: the Prometheus gauge is not built, and nothing probes `/ready` yet: Squire's `health.php` (Citadel's Health Check and the compose healthcheck) asks `/up`, so only point a traffic probe at `/ready` where `schedule:run` really runs.

### W24. Run migrations exactly once per release [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#w24-run-migrations-exactly-once-per-release)

**Practice:** Use a Job, a pre-deploy hook (Coolify "Pre-deployment Command"), or `migrate --isolated`. Never run `migrate` in a per-replica entrypoint.

**Why:** Parallel replicas race on schema changes.

**Stack:** `Checked`. On Citadel the release step runs `php artisan migrate --force` (`deploy/scripts/release.sh:550`) once per release, from the first-release hook (`deploy/deployments/001-first-release.sh`, which only calls the release script) and the Quick Update post-script (`deploy/scripts/release.sh:7`); Citadel's entrypoint runs no artisan command (`deploy/.squire/fallback/citadel-apache-entrypoint`). Off Citadel the portable image migrates only in its `migrate` role (`deploy/.squire/portable/squire-entrypoint.sh:157-167`), a one-shot service the `web`, `worker` and `scheduler` services wait for (`service_completed_successfully`, `deploy/docker-compose.squire.yml:194-235`). `tests/Feature/MigrateOncePerReleaseTest.php` fails when a kit update moves `migrate` anywhere else. PROCTOR's `entrypoint-migrate` check still warns on the portable entrypoint (it lets a `migrate)` case branch through, not a `run_migrate` function the branch calls), so that one warning is expected; the portability CI job does not run the `migrate` role, but migrates its own test database once, in its own container, before the two replicas start (`setup_command`, `.gitlab-ci.yml:113`).

### How to read the tags [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#how-to-read-the-tags)

Each practice ends with exactly one tag.

| Tag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Enforced` | WELD's code does it or refuses to run without it, and a test covers it. |
| `Checked` | PROCTOR or CI warns or fails. |
| `Documented` | Written down in the README or a config file, with no check behind it. |
| `Not yet` | A gap. |

### Related [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queues-and-scheduling.html#related)

- [App structure](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/app-structure.html)
- [The container contract](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/container-contract.html)
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html)

## Quick start [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#quick-start)

This page takes a fresh copy of WELD from a folder to a running, checked app on your machine.

One command strikes the spark; the containers do the welding. Docker is the only prerequisite: PHP and Node run in the containers, so the host needs neither.

### Steps [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#steps)

1. Bring the stack up:
   PowerShell
   ```powershell
   .\bin\weld.ps1 up
   ```
   macOS / Linux
   ```sh
   bin/weld.sh up
   ```
   Expected: `up` copies `.env.example` to `.env` if it is missing, installs the PHP and Node dependencies in the containers, starts the app and Vite, generates the app key if it is not set, and runs the migrations.
2. Open [http://localhost:8000](http://localhost:8000). Expected: the app, served by the local stack.
3. Run the doctor:
   PowerShell
   ```powershell
   .\bin\weld.ps1 doctor
   ```
   macOS / Linux
   ```sh
   bin/weld.sh doctor
   ```
   Expected: one line per check, PASS or WARN or FAIL; exit code 1 when anything FAILs. A good bead is a quiet one: all PASS and nothing to say.
4. Run the checks:
   PowerShell
   ```powershell
   .\bin\weld.ps1 test
   ```
   macOS / Linux
   ```sh
   bin/weld.sh test
   ```
   Expected: `composer ci` runs in the app container: validate, tests, Pint, PHPStan level 8, the agent-ready check and audit.

### The subcommands [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#the-subcommands)

The same subcommands work on every OS:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `up` | Bring the whole stack up, as above |
| `down` | Stop and remove the containers, and clear Vite's `public/hot` |
| `test` | Run `composer ci` in the app container |
| `doctor` | Run `php artisan weld:doctor` in the app container |
| `logs` | Follow the container logs |

### Run it like Citadel [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#run-it-like-citadel)

The steps above are the everyday bench: the stock PHP image, SQLite and Vite reloading as you type, and Sail or plain Docker Compose work too. Parity does not replace them. When "it works here" has to mean "it works on Citadel", run the same folder on Citadel's own machinery with [Parity](https://parity.apps.wayne.edu/): Citadel's PHP image with its `php.ini` and `vhost.conf`, Citadel's proxy in front adding `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Forwarded-Proto`, and MySQL 5.6, the version of Citadel's shared database server. Parity is one program for Windows, macOS and Linux on Podman (recommended) or Docker. It needs no PHP on your computer and adds one file to the app, `parity.json`. Install it once from [its site](https://parity.apps.wayne.edu/), with no administrator needed. On Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://parity.apps.wayne.edu/install.ps1 | iex
```

On macOS and Linux:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://parity.apps.wayne.edu/install.sh | sh
```

1. Stop the Compose stack (`down`), so Vite's dev server is not in the way, and build the front end once, because Citadel serves built assets:
   ```sh
   docker compose run --rm vite npm run build
   ```
   Expected: `down` also clears `public/hot`, the note Vite's dev server leaves so pages load from it. Left behind, it gives you a blank page under Parity.
2. Check this computer, then write the app's Citadel settings:
   ```sh
   parity check
   parity init --mysql
   ```
   Expected: `parity check` prints one line per finding, with the fix under each one that needs it. `parity init` writes `parity.json`; `--mysql` is Citadel's "MySQL: yes".
3. Add one line to `parity.json`, under `"mode"`, so the health check asks Laravel's `/up`, as Squire's `health.php` does on Citadel:
   ```json
   "health_check": "curl -fsS -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1/up",
   ```
   Parity's default asks the front page, which needs the sessions table, and that table arrives with the migration in the next step. Without this line the first `parity up` waits five minutes and fails.
4. Bring it up, migrate as Citadel would, and test it:
   ```sh
   parity up
   parity shell --user citadel php artisan migrate
   parity test
   ```
   Expected: `parity up` builds the app behind the proxy and prints its address ([http://localhost:8080](http://localhost:8080) unless you pick a port). On a fresh database the front page answers 500 until the migration runs, so the first `parity up` ends on a warning that says so; on Windows its proxy step can time out on that page instead. Carry on with the migration: `parity test` is the word that counts. Your folder is mounted where Citadel mounts it, so an edit shows on the next request. The app gets Laravel's `DB_*` settings for the local MySQL, so `.env` keeps SQLite for the everyday bench. `parity test` asks the running app what Citadel's users would; `parity down` stops it and keeps the data.

A folder on the Windows disk is slow inside the container: in the 2026-11-09 proof run a page took about 10 seconds, and `php artisan --version` 9 seconds against a quarter of a second from the container's own disk. Slow, but it holds.

No Citadel image on this computer yet? `parity image get` downloads it with your own git.wayne.edu access and checks it byte for byte, and `parity up --fallback` builds a labeled stand-in from the official PHP image meanwhile. Parity 0.1.0 is live, and [its docs](https://parity.apps.wayne.edu/docs/) have the rest. It takes over local runs from the parity kit in Squire. Same app, same folder, now in Citadel's own image: the bead looks identical under the hood, because it is the same hood.

### What you built [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#what-you-built)

You have WELD running locally in Docker: the app and Vite in containers, `.env` copied from `.env.example`, the app key generated and the migrations run. That is the whole Wayne State app stack joined into one application, with sign-in, security headers, checks, coding standards, CI and the WayneUI interface already hooked up. Open the app and every page you see (the welcome page, the dashboard, settings) is drawn by WayneUI's components, light or dark to match your device.

### Next steps [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#next-steps)

- [Make it yours](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/making-weld-yours.html): rename the parts that still say WELD (the composer name, the app name, the site title and the git remote), give the copy its own key and re-run the checks, then strip WELD's product files and adopt Sourdough so `feed` keeps working.
- [Check your setup](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/check-your-setup.html): what the doctor reports, joint by joint.
- [What is welded in](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/whats-welded-in.html): the parts and what each does in the app.
- [Run it like Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#run-it-like-citadel): the same folder on Citadel's image, proxy and MySQL 5.6, through Parity.
- [Citadel limits](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel-limits.html): the platform facts an app design depends on, with their sources.
- [Running WELD off Citadel](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/running-off-citadel.html): for when the destination is somewhere other than a laptop.

### Related [#](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#related)

- [Install](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html)
